Package de.nexus.antixray.api.event

Class XRayAlertEvent

java.lang.Object
org.bukkit.event.Event
org.bukkit.event.player.PlayerEvent
de.nexus.antixray.api.event.XRayAlertEvent
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.bukkit.event.Cancellable
public class XRayAlertEvent extends org.bukkit.event.player.PlayerEvent implements org.bukkit.event.Cancellable
Called when the x-ray detection is about to raise an alert for a player, before anything is sent.

An alert is due when a player digs into a bait vein and is then at or above both thresholds of xray-detection.alert within the detection window, and the cooldown since the previous alert is over. The getters carry the values of the placeholders that config.yml offers for alert commands: {player} and {uuid} (PlayerEvent.getPlayer()), {world} (getWorld()), {x}, {y}, {z}, {veins} (getBaitVeins()), {blocks} (getMinedBlocks()) and {rate} (getRate()), plus the length of the window.

Cancelling

A cancelled alert did not happen:
  • nothing is sent: no console line, no staff chat message, no command from xray-detection.commands, no Discord message and no line in detections.log;
  • it is not counted: /nax stats and MiningStats.getAlertCount() stay as they were;
  • the cooldown (xray-detection.alert.cooldown-minutes) does not start.
The bait veins the player has hit stay counted. A player whose alert was cancelled is therefore still above the thresholds, and the event is called again for the next bait vein that player digs into, until an alert goes through or the player drops below the thresholds. A listener that cancels the event in order to send its own notification has to limit how often it does so; a listener that only wants to react in addition should leave the event alone.

So that a server owner can find out why alerts never arrive, NexusAntiXRay keeps two traces that say nothing about the alert itself: the first cancelled alert of a server run is noted in the log together with the plugins that listen to this event, and the number of cancelled alerts is part of the support report (/nax report).

Thread

The event is synchronous. It is called on the thread that ticks the player: the server thread, on Folia the region thread that owns the player. It is never called from a network or ray tracing thread.

It is called from inside the BlockBreakEvent of the block that crossed the threshold (priority MONITOR). Do not kick, teleport or otherwise remove the player right in the handler; schedule that for the next tick, as NexusAntiXRay does with its own commands.

Since:
1.0.0
